clue.text: Lightweight insect is caught nipping maiden

indicators.note: the insect is said to have caught the next piece, so it closes round it

parts.note: a fly is an insect

indicators.note: to nip is to pinch, so the word is grips the maiden letter between its own

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A small bug gets trapped while biting a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is read as letters, not a verb: the maiden sits inside them, and that pair together sits inside the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy and lightweight are synonyms for something insubstantial or slight.

clue.text: Party female with religious glibness

parts.note: unction is fervour, or a smooth affected religious manner

explanation.surface: A woman at a gathering is smoothly pious.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is a formal social gathering, so it means a party.

clue.text: It's sort of white and gold inside plant

indicators.note: inside places the word for gold within the plant

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A white flower has a golden centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a creamy shade of white, named after elephant tusk.

clue.text: Sister carrying adequate test-piece

indicators.note: carrying means the sister abbreviation holds the next word inside it

parts.note: ample means enough, adequate

explanation.surface: A nun carries enough for an exam piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A sampler is an embroidered piece a learner sews to show skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is a piece of needlework done to demonstrate skill, a kind of test piece.

clue.text: Boats that can sail on account of blows

definitions.meaning: fishing boats with sails, a kind of single-masted coaster

explanation.surface: Sailing vessels are named after the hits they take.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is both a small sailing fishing boat and a sharp slap, so the plural fits each sense.

clue.text: Clown having brandy and water in France

parts.note: marc is a brandy made from grape residue
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A clown drinks brandy and water while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcel Marceau was the famous French mime artist, here called a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Marceau was a celebrated mime whose character Bip was a white-faced clown.

clue.text: Moron came to waste our time

indicators.note: laying something to waste wrecks it, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: A fool arrives to fritter away our hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the dating system for the present age, the time we live in.

clue.text: Stream created by ship going round lake

indicators.note: going round means the ship abbreviation encloses the lake

parts.note: SS is steamship
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A creek forms where a vessel sails around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream can mean a continuous succession, as does a series of events.

clue.text: A learner next to where he should be is relaxed

parts.note: a player at his best is in form, which is where he ought to be
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A trainee driver feels at ease beside the spot he belongs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' simply joins the pieces; 'where he should be' is a cryptic pointer to IN FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual and easy-going, which is what relaxed describes.

clue.text: Very courageous in the ordeal, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone shows great bravery during a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionhearted means brave as a lion, very courageous.

clue.text: Comment on one of the Gospels

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Mark is one of the four Gospels of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A critic writes notes about a book of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written comment, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lodge with paths ultimately leading to river

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word paths

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A cabin sits where walking routes end at a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to stay there as a guest or resident, a verb synonym.

clue.text: What we hear excited travellers from Calais say? That must be examined

indicators.note: what we hear signals that the cry of the travellers is taken by its sound

parts.note: ferry passengers from Calais spotting the English port cry out Look, Dover!

explanation.surface: Ferry passengers shout on sighting land, and their cry needs scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossing from Calais, passengers would shout 'Look, Dover!', which sounds like the answer. 'That must be' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looked something over is to have examined or inspected it.

clue.text: Oe'r such you may wander when National Trust gets involved

definitions.text: Oe'r such you may wander when National Trust gets involved

indicators.note: wandering letters move about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British charity that owns historic estates

explanation.surface: Visitors roam the grounds of a stately home looked after by a conservation charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of OERSUCHYOU plus NT gives the answer, and the whole clue describes a stately home that visitors may roam once the National Trust, a British heritage charity, runs it.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Trust owns and opens many grand rural mansions, which visitors stroll around.

clue.text: Suffering aunt gets to recover without medical help?

indicators.note: suffering hints at the word aunt being battered into new shape

parts.note: to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: An ill aunt manages to get better without a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' makes NATU from AUNT; 'gets to' is a link. The question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover naturally is to heal by nature alone, without treatment.

clue.text: Sloppy consul, about 51, a contemptible fellow

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the number
sloppy suggests careless, so the word consul is jumbled

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A careless diplomat of about fifty-one is despicable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, not a vague 'roughly'. A scullion was a lowly kitchen drudge, so the word became an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Scullion, once a menial kitchen servant, is used as a term of contempt for a base fellow.

clue.text: Two sailors and a hairy man going to church for something to eat

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and two give a pair of them
a tar is a sailor, and two give a pair of them
in Genesis, Esau is described as a hairy man
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pair of seamen and a shaggy fellow head off to a service, then eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' joins the pieces in order. Esau, Jacob's brother in the Bible, is called 'a hairy man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce is a condiment served with fish, so it counts as food, loosely.

clue.text: Fast male animal pursued by a desperate man in comic

indicators.note: pursued by puts the following pieces after the first

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
Desperate Dan is a character in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A male beast is chased by a frantic cartoon figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting, so it names a fast.

clue.text: Resent a drunk becoming serious

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so these letters are reeled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy grows bitter and then solemn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and serious are synonyms describing a sincere, grave manner.

clue.text: Meaning that comes here from abroad

definitions.meaning: significance, as in the ... of a speech
goods brought in from a foreign country

explanation.surface: Significance arrives from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Import means both significance and goods brought in from another country.

clue.text: Naughty kid beginning to reform, one adult almost? Approval shown

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of reform

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: mature means grown-up, adult

explanation.surface: A mischievous child starts to behave, nearly grown up, and earns approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MATURE to MATUR. An imprimatur is an official licence to print, from Latin 'let it be printed'; 'shown' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprimatur is an official sanction, so it means approval or authorisation.

clue.text: Deal offers second drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A bargain comes with a second round at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale is a deal in which goods change hands for money.

clue.text: Indistinct sound was odd outside church

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters sit around the church abbreviation
odd suggests strangeness, so the word was is rearranged

explanation.surface: A muffled noise was strange outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' signals the jumble of the three-letter word. The schwa is the unstressed vowel, as in the first letter of 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A schwa is the neutral unstressed vowel, a vague indistinct sound in speech.

clue.text: Dismissed when sounding impudent

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for impudent is taken by how it is said

parts.note: bold can mean cheeky or impudent

explanation.surface: A cheeky person gets sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman bowled is out, dismissed by a ball hitting the wicket. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bowled is one way for a cricket batsman to be dismissed, sent off the field.

clue.text: Dried hay can be turned into coloured thatch

indicators.note: turning letters into something else rearranges them

explanation.surface: Dried hay could be made into a roof, painted a new colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatch is a jokey word for a head of hair, so coloured thatch is hair that has been dyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is slang for a head of hair, so coloured thatch is hair tinted artificially.

clue.text: Having a go is stressful

explanation.surface: Making an attempt is exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying is both the present participle of attempt and an adjective meaning taxing.

clue.text: Make too many demands on son going to school

parts.note: to school is to train or teach

explanation.surface: A boy heads off to lessons, and it overtaxes him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' just joins the pieces; 'school' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain something is to overtax it, pushing beyond what it can bear.
